one_line: Anthropic launches models and IPO plans; Nvidia scandal triggers probes; EU targets AI addiction; Disney partners with Adobe.

themes.title: Anthropic launches new models, eyes IPO
themes.text: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, offering faster output and improved coding, reasoning, and vision, priced at $8‑$40 per million tokens. The company also prepared for its IPO, sending and retracting filing pricing details and planning a live‑stream event with CEO Dario Amodei and JPMorgan’s Jamie Dimon.

themes.title: Nvidia scandal sparks investigations
themes.text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, leading to a board‑led investigation and his withdrawal from the ElevenLabs Summit. Following the controversy, U.S. investigators transferred a probe of alleged AI‑chip diversion to the Justice Department after Nvidia contacted the agency.

themes.title: EU drafts Digital Fairness Act
themes.text: The European Commission will consider the Digital Fairness Act, which would require companies to let adults disable addictive features and would target AI systems that simulate relationships, alongside measures on manipulative design and hard‑to‑cancel subscriptions. The draft estimates consumer harm at €7.9 billion annually.

themes.title: Disney partners with Adobe on AI
themes.text: Disney and Adobe signed a multiyear agreement to develop proprietary, artist‑led generative AI models using Adobe Firefly Foundry for Disney’s production pipeline, including theme parks, cruise line, and ESPN graphics. The deal gives Disney early access to the AI technology.
